questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Making international friends, learing the language.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language. The city itself. The closeness to home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the paperwork around it was a nightmare (especially with the semester being different than in Denmark) but the trip itself was great.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It's not always easy to find the information you want on the schools website as it can be very confusing. But I found that I wanted a lot of information before hand that I didn't actually need. Everything you need to know (academically) thay will tell you upan arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They did an online introduction "seminar" for incoming students. Also there are introduction days at campus where they introduce you to everything. Also they make it clear that you can always go to the Erasmus office with questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to find housing. It has become incredibly hard in recent years. I reccomend using WG-gesucht and verious Facaebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Campus is really far away from the city center, so you are almost always going to live far away from campus if you want to live close to the city. Be aware of the fact that the student housing offered is very often quite far away from the cuty center and some of them are hard to reach by prublic transportation. Just check that you whan you apply for them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Student housing get's booked out incredibly fast!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy but confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You basically register for a lot of different courses when the semester starts but you don't need to take all of them. So you spent the first few weeks shopping between courses attending different lectures and then you choose what you want to take. Then you go on the online course registration and sign off the courses you don't want anyways.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty succesfull. Even if you don't get certain classes you want (or maybe realise too late that you want other classes than the ones you signed up for) you can always talk to the professers personally and ask if you can join the class anyways. So I ended up getting all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sometimes a class you thought was good, isn't what you thought it was going to be once you try it out, so register for a lot more classes than you think you need and try them out! That way you have backup options. You can always sign off them again.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's pretty diverse if you are willing to take classes in German too. The classes in English offered (at the bachelors level) is not all that impressive in my openion. But definitely not bad still! They just have so many good courses in German.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found that they were slightly easier than back home. But yuo get very little assistance with the exam writing, which is where it gets hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at Freie is very "class based". So most courses are seminars and not lectures. You do a lot more group work and depating in class, and the lecturers rarely do long presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Migration and Integration: main teories and their empirical applications (masters level)
Comparative European Politics
Rechtsextremismus in Deutschland
Einführung in die Bewegungs- und Protestforschung

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The teacher in Comparative European Politics is really good! And Rechtsextremismus in Deutschland is so interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No really any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I was surprised to find that you pay a one time fee to the university and than you have "free" public transportation during the whole semester.
Eating out and buying groceries is slightly less expensive than in Denmark. But the night life is a bit more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not very many options. Sports clubs filled up very fast. And I was not aware of many other social clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I'm honestly not vey sure. Not many that Erasmus students were made aware of or encuraged to take part in.
Erasmus arranged parties and some events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would very much like to recommend doing the Vorkurs in German. The presemester intensive course is where I met litterally all my friends during my stay. And so many students take these, that if you arrive afterwards it's almost hard to mingle with the people who did the course. Because you become very close very fast with the people you do the course with. Would ABSOLUTELY recommend!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Potsdam. Thats very nice. During christitmas I visited christmas markets in near by cities like Dresden and Leipzig. That can be done in a single day trip. Also every weekend there are major fleemarkets around the cities, which are really good and really popular.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Danes and Germans are a lot alike.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get a tandemparter. That's pretty much the only local student i befriended.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They only ose cash for everything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do the German presemester intensive course (Vorkurs) - even if you don't want to learn German! It's the best decision I've made in a long time.
2. Begin looking for housing early. Exhaust all sources! It's easier if you know somebody, who knows sombody. But also be patient. A lot of people only just post apartments very shortly before they want it rented out.
3. It's going to be such a fun semester, but be very aware of the many challenges it entails that the semester is not the same in Germany as in Denmark. It means A LOT of confusion, and paperwork and bureaucratic stuff. You have to be willing to put in some extra work.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Mostly the people I met. But also the feel of the city and practicing the language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the bureaucratic stuff and the planning. It's really hard when you get home after the fall semester and the spring semster back home is already started and you have to finish up exams from you semester in Berlin along side following classes in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
